lessons.titleZh: 不把熱情與生活意義耗空

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Choose work that pays well without draining the soul.

brief.meaningEn: Without exhausting a person’s enjoyment, sense of meaning or emotional energy, in a figurative description.
brief.meaningZh: 以比喻描述，不把一個人的樂趣、意義感或情感精力耗空。
brief.grammar: work that pays without draining the soul; without + -ing marks an effect avoided. Soul is a figurative image of personal vitality or meaning, not a literal liquid container or a clinical description.
brief.register: A creative emotional-depletion image. A demanding or tiring day is not by itself evidence of losing all meaning; describe the person’s own experience and the practical conditions.
brief.boundaryZh: 仍可有辛苦工作或疲累日子；不要把沒有任何壓力當成唯一理解，也不能單憑高薪或職銜判定情緒感受。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把人物的感受替換成診斷，也不把重視工作當成可以無限增加工作量的理由。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把意義感與實際日常連起來，提出有範圍的調整，而不空泛要求永不疲累。

listening.promptZh: 人物的描述怎樣同時保留辛苦與意義？

options.en: The work could be tiring while she still found enjoyment and energy for her own drawing.
options.zh: 工作可以累，但她仍有樂趣，也有精力畫自己的作品。

options.en: She described a job with no tiring days and no difficult tasks.
options.zh: 她描述了一份沒有疲累日子，也沒有困難任務的工作。

options.en: She said the salary was the only valued part and that she had stopped wanting to draw.
options.zh: 她說薪酬是唯一重視的部分，而且已不想畫畫。

options.en: The account gives only the studio’s pay figure, without describing how she experienced the work.
options.zh: 敘述只提供工作室的薪酬數字，沒有說她怎樣感受工作。

listening.explanationZh: 題目有具體樂趣及自己的創作精力，也承認疲累；不能把比喻改成完全沒有困難，或只有薪酬資料。
listening.en: Her work at the small studio paid the rent without draining the soul: she still enjoyed solving problems with colleagues and had energy to draw for herself, even after a tiring day.
listening.zh: 她在小工作室的工作能付房租，也沒有把熱情與生活意義耗空：即使一天很累，她仍享受與同事解決問題，也有精力畫自己的作品。

reply.promptEn: What made the studio work feel compatible with her own life?
reply.promptZh: 甚麼讓工作室的工作感覺仍能配合她自己的生活？

options.en: It paid the rent without draining the soul, since she still enjoyed the collaboration and her own drawing.
options.zh: 它能付房租，也沒有把熱情與意義耗空，因她仍享受合作及自己的創作。

options.en: The income came alongside useful collaboration and energy for something she valued outside the job.
options.zh: 收入之外，她仍有有意義的合作，以及投入工作以外重視之事的精力。

options.en: She did not have to describe every day as easy to find the work rewarding.
options.zh: 她不用把每天都說成輕鬆，也仍能覺得工作有價值。

options.en: The account links work with enjoyment and a continuing personal practice, not pay alone.
options.zh: 敘述把工作連到樂趣及持續的個人創作，不只薪酬。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留本人具體的樂趣與生活，不只按薪酬猜感受，也不要求每天都輕鬆。

scene.promptZh: 人物薪酬高，卻明說整周工作後感到空洞，已不想碰原本珍惜的寫作；評論只因待遇好，便套用「不會耗空心靈」。哪句最好？

options.en: High pay alone does not show work continuing without draining the soul when the person describes a loss of meaning and interest.
options.zh: 人物描述意義感及興趣流失時，單是高薪不足以顯示工作沒有把熱情與生活意義耗空。

options.en: The account describes her enjoying the work and returning eagerly to her personal writing.
options.zh: 敘述說她享受工作，並熱切回到自己的寫作。

options.en: The person’s own experience is not relevant once the salary has been described as high.
options.zh: 一旦薪酬被描述為高，人物本人的感受就與判斷無關。

scene.explanationZh: 要按本人描述的感受理解，不以待遇代替，也不自行加入仍享受寫作的說法。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「without draining the soul」得出？

options.en: The description avoids a figurative loss of meaning or vitality.
options.zh: 描述指避免了比喻中的意義感或活力流失。

options.en: The person never feels tired or faces a demanding day.
options.zh: 那人從不疲累，也不會遇上辛苦日子。

options.en: The surrounding account can explain what remains meaningful to the person.
options.zh: 前後敘述可以交代，那人仍覺得甚麼有意義。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有被耗空，不是每天毫不費力；這是感受與意義的比喻，不是診斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然她仍喜歡這份工作，就再加幾晚也不用問吧？」你想保留有意義與可持續的安排。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Continuing without draining the soul depends on what she can actually sustain; enjoying the work is not agreement to extra evenings, so we should ask.
options.zh: 能繼續而不把熱情耗空，要看她實際能承擔甚麼；喜歡工作不等於同意額外晚上，我們應先問。

options.en: I would use her enjoyment as agreement to the extra rota before discussing her availability.
options.zh: 我會在討論她是否有空之前，把她的樂趣當成同意額外輪值。

options.en: I would judge whether the extra work suits her only by the pay, rather than ask about its effect on her own time.
options.zh: 我只會按薪酬判斷額外工作是否適合她，不問對她自己時間的影響。

dialogue.explanationZh: 具體時間、意願及生活影響仍需要本人說明；不能把熱情當成額外承諾，也不能只看報酬。

speaking.en: I want to do useful work without draining the soul, with time to think, collaborate and keep the personal interests that matter to me.
speaking.zh: 我想做有用的工作，也不把熱情與生活意義耗空，能有時間思考、合作，並保留對自己重要的個人興趣。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把意義感連到可描述的生活條件。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你喜歡工作坊的有薪創作工作，但這幾周幾乎全被安排接待，原本議定的畫畫時段也消失了。你要向負責人提出商量：可否輪流接待、保留一段已議定的創作時間；不要假定有人已答應代班，也不要求工作永遠沒有繁忙。用一至兩句英文寫實際請求。

examples.en: I want to keep doing this paid work without draining the soul, so could we discuss rotating reception duties and restoring an agreed drawing session? I value the workshop, but the current rota has left no time for the creative part I joined to do.
examples.zh: 我想繼續這份有薪工作，也不把熱情與生活意義耗空，所以我們可否商量輪流接待，並恢復一節已議定的畫畫時間？我重視工作坊，但目前輪值已沒有時間做我當初加入要做的創作。

examples.en: The work matters to me, but I need a way to continue without draining the soul. Could we look together at reception cover and the drawing time we agreed, before assuming the present allocation can continue unchanged?
examples.zh: 這份工作對我重要，但我需要一種不把熱情與生活意義耗空的繼續方法。我們可否一起看看接待人手及已議定的畫畫時間，不先假定現有分配可以照舊持續？

glossary.zh: 已議定的一節畫畫時間

writing.selfCheckZh: 請求要說明原本工作價值及目前分配的具體問題，再邀請一起商量；不把熱情當無限人手，也不替其他人承諾代班。

takeaways.en: The character hopes to earn a living without draining the soul, so she asks which parts of the new role would leave room for the work she values.
takeaways.zh: 角色希望賺取生活費而不把熱情與生活意義耗空，所以她詢問新角色哪些部分仍能保留重視的工作。

takeaways.en: Their plan was to run the small project without draining the soul, keeping honest conversations about the workload rather than relying only on enthusiasm.
takeaways.zh: 他們計劃經營小項目而不把熱情與意義耗空，誠實討論工作量，不只靠熱情。

lessons.titleZh: 只為擁有權力而行使權力

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Good leadership is not authority for its own sake.

brief.meaningEn: Authority valued or asserted as an end in itself, rather than to serve a useful shared purpose.
brief.meaningZh: 把權力本身當目的來追求或行使，而不是為了有用的共同目的。
brief.grammar: authority for its own sake; its refers to authority. Contrast a justified coordinating role with control pursued merely to display or preserve power. For its own sake does not make every use of authority unjustified.
brief.register: A conventional for-its-own-sake construction applied to power, often critical in this context. The whole authority phrase is not a separate opaque idiom; the surrounding account should establish the purpose or lack of it.
brief.boundaryZh: 有規則、分工或審核，不一定就是只為權力；要看有沒有合理目的、範圍及實際需要，不能只按職銜猜動機。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把不接受多餘控制，寫成不需要任何協調，也不因是領導者就假定每個程序都有用。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清協調目的與權力展示，並以具體做法描寫角色如何調整。

listening.promptZh: 敘述者質疑哪種目的？是否反對所有協調？

options.en: The concern was power being displayed as its own purpose, while coordination could still be necessary.
options.zh: 顧慮是以展示權力本身為目的，而協調仍可能有需要。

options.en: The narrator said shared equipment should have no coordinating arrangements at all.
options.zh: 敘述者說，共同器材完全不應有協調安排。

options.en: The chair explained a specific equipment conflict that the extra approval would resolve.
options.zh: 主席解釋了額外批准會解決哪項具體器材衝突。

options.en: The account describes removing an unnecessary approval step rather than adding one.
options.zh: 敘述描述的是取消多餘批准，而不是增加。

listening.explanationZh: 主席給的只是顯示誰作主的理由；這不等於敘述者否定共享器材仍有合理協調需要。
listening.en: The chair added another approval step and explained it only as a way to show who was in charge; the narrator questioned authority for its own sake, not the need to coordinate the shared equipment.
listening.zh: 主席加了一重批准，卻只解釋是為了顯示誰作主；敘述者質疑的是只為權力而行權，不是共同器材不需要協調。

reply.promptEn: What was the narrator questioning about the extra approval?
reply.promptZh: 敘述者在質疑額外批准的哪一點？

options.en: It appeared to be authority for its own sake, justified only by displaying who was in charge.
options.zh: 它看來是只為權力而行權，理由只是展示誰作主。

options.en: The stated reason did not identify a shared practical need for another step.
options.zh: 已說明的理由，沒有指出再加一步的共同實際需要。

options.en: The concern was the purpose of the control, not the existence of every coordinating rule.
options.zh: 顧慮在控制的目的，不是在於任何協調規則的存在。

options.en: The narrator wanted a reason beyond showing the chair’s position.
options.zh: 敘述者想知道，除了顯示主席地位以外還有甚麼理由。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都把質疑放在程序的目的，不一概否定規則或協調。

scene.promptZh: 器材管理員要求歸還時簽一個簡短欄位，並解釋這讓下一組知道物品是否齊全；規則只限借用器材，沒有要求批准無關選擇。有人只因有簽名，就稱為純粹權力。哪句最好？

options.en: A bounded return record with a stated shared purpose is not by itself authority for its own sake.
options.zh: 有明確共同目的、範圍有限的歸還記錄，本身不等於只為權力而行權。

options.en: The account gives no reason for the signature beyond showing the manager’s rank.
options.zh: 敘述沒有提供簽名理由，只有顯示管理員地位。

options.en: The rule is described as requiring approval for choices unrelated to borrowed equipment.
options.zh: 規則被描述為要求批准與借用器材無關的選擇。

scene.explanationZh: 規則有明確用途及範圍；不能只看有簽名便猜成展示權力，也不能擴大成題目沒有的控制。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能從批評 authority for its own sake 得出？

options.en: The speaker objects to power being treated as its own purpose.
options.zh: 說話者反對把權力本身當成目的。

options.en: The speaker must reject any leadership, coordination or useful rule.
options.zh: 說話者必定反對任何領導、協調或有用規則。

options.en: A concrete context can distinguish justified oversight from control without a relevant purpose.
options.zh: 具體情境可以區分有理由的監督，與沒有相關目的的控制。

contrast.explanationZh: 反對權力只為權力，不等於否定所有規則；要看實際作用和範圍。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只要是主席加的程序，就不用再問它幫甚麼吧？」你想理解程序的作用。哪個回應最好？

options.en: We should ask what the extra step achieves; questioning authority for its own sake does not stop us keeping a rule that serves a clear shared need.
options.zh: 我們應問額外一步達到甚麼；質疑只為權力而行權，不妨礙保留能服務明確共同需要的規則。

options.en: I would keep the extra step on the strength of the title, without asking what problem it addresses.
options.zh: 我會只憑職銜保留額外程序，不問它處理甚麼問題。

options.en: I would remove the existing return record as well, without considering the equipment-sharing reason already given.
options.zh: 我會連現有歸還記錄也取消，不考慮已說明的共享器材理由。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應逐項看目的及證據；既不按職銜自動接受，也不因反對一重程序就一併取消已知有用的安排。

speaking.en: I want coordination that serves the project, not authority for its own sake, so I would ask what each approval step actually helps us do.
speaking.zh: 我想要服務項目的協調，不是只為權力而行權，所以會問每重批准實際幫我們做甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把程序連到共同目的。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在續寫小說結尾。新任組長原本要求每張海報都由他決定顏色，後來發現這只是怕自己看來沒用，反而耽誤了大家。他現在撤回那項額外批准，仍保留已議定的日期及場地資料核對，讓設計者自己選顏色。用一至兩句英文實際寫這個轉折，不只評論「好領導」。

examples.en: He crossed out the colour-approval line, recognising that he had been seeking authority for its own sake rather than helping the posters get made. The designers could choose their colours, while the agreed check of dates and venue details remained.
examples.zh: 他刪去顏色批准那一行，承認自己一直只為權力而求權力，不是在幫海報完成。設計者可以自行選顏色，原已議定的日期及場地資料核對則仍保留。

examples.en: His fear of looking unnecessary had turned the colour choice into authority for its own sake, so he handed that decision back to the designers. He kept the shared facts check, this time able to explain what it was for.
examples.zh: 他怕自己顯得沒有用，把選顏色變成只為權力而行權，於是把那個決定交回設計者。他保留共同資料核對，這次卻能解釋它有甚麼用途。

writing.selfCheckZh: 續寫要有撤回多餘控制及保留有用核對的實際轉折，交代人物承認的動機；不要把它寫成取消所有協調，也不只空泛稱讚角色。

takeaways.en: The organiser asked whether the new signature served a real need or had become authority for its own sake.
takeaways.zh: 主辦者問，新簽名要求是在回應實際需要，還是已變成只為權力而行權。

takeaways.en: Her account contrasts useful coordination with authority for its own sake, using a specific delay rather than the leader’s title as evidence.
takeaways.zh: 她的敘述把有用協調與只為權力而行權作對比，以具體延誤、而非領導職銜作證據。

english.evidence: Conventional for-its-own-sake intrinsic-purpose construction applied to authority; critical application does not condemn every rule. Main extra approval justified only as displaying rank, inverse bounded equipment-return record has an explicit function, final actual fictional turning point withdraws colour control while preserving agreed factual checks, moving from evaluating a rule to depicting a changed leader’s action.

lessons.titleZh: 不經判斷便服從

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A healthy team does not require blind obedience.

brief.meaningEn: Following instructions without questioning or judging their reasons or consequences.
brief.meaningZh: 不質疑或判斷指示的理由、後果，便照做。
brief.grammar: blind obedience to a person/rule; demand/reject blind obedience. Obedience is uncountable here. Blind is an established figurative adjective for unexamined belief or action.
brief.register: A conventional adjective–noun collocation for unthinking compliance. Following an instruction after considering its purpose is not automatically blind obedience.
brief.boundaryZh: 需要判斷的是有沒有理解與檢視，不是只看有否照做；合理規則可以在了解後遵守，質疑也不等於否定所有合作。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把獨立判斷寫成每件事都必須反對，也不因相信對方就當不用看自己正答應甚麼。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清理解後合作與不經檢視照做，並提出具體問題而不空泛抗拒。

listening.promptZh: 她希望團隊怎樣參與？期限是否因此被取消？

options.en: The team should examine doubtful captions and give reasons, while keeping an agreed deadline.
options.zh: 團隊應檢視可疑圖說並說明理由，同時保留議定期限。

options.en: The team should accept every caption because the editor’s title makes checking unnecessary.
options.zh: 團隊應因編輯職銜而接受每段圖說，不再需要核對。

options.en: The editor withdrew the deadline so that the team would never need to coordinate the issue.
options.zh: 編輯取消了期限，讓團隊不再需要協調這一期出版。

options.en: The editor asked for agreement without allowing the team to explain why a caption seemed doubtful.
options.zh: 編輯要求同意，不讓團隊解釋為甚麼覺得圖說可疑。

listening.explanationZh: 她要有依據的參與，不是不經檢視照做；保留共同期限，也顯示這並非取消合作安排。
listening.en: The editor rejected blind obedience: she asked the team to question doubtful captions and explain their evidence, while still agreeing a clear deadline for the issue.
listening.zh: 編輯不接受不經判斷便服從：她請團隊質疑可疑圖說並解釋證據，同時仍議定清楚的出版期限。

reply.promptEn: What kind of cooperation did the editor want?
reply.promptZh: 編輯想要甚麼樣的合作？

options.en: She wanted reasoned participation, not blind obedience to doubtful captions.
options.zh: 她想要有理由的參與，不是對可疑圖說不經判斷便服從。

options.en: The team could question the wording and explain what evidence supported a change.
options.zh: 團隊可以質疑字句，解釋甚麼證據支持修改。

options.en: She kept a shared deadline while asking people to think about what they published.
options.zh: 她保留共同期限，同時請大家思考自己發布的內容。

options.en: Working together meant giving reasons, not accepting a caption merely because someone senior supplied it.
options.zh: 合作是提出理由，不是只因資深者提供圖說就接受。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述有理由的共同工作；不把服從與合作畫上等號，也不把質疑當成取消期限。

scene.promptZh: 義工先問清物品歸還表的用途，理解它可讓下一組查到借用品，再按已議定方式填寫。評論只因他照規則做，便稱為盲從。哪句最好？

options.en: Following a rule after asking about and understanding its purpose is not by itself blind obedience.
options.zh: 先詢問並理解用途後遵守規則，本身不等於不經判斷便服從。

options.en: The account says he filled the form without considering why it was needed.
options.zh: 敘述說，他沒有考慮表格為甚麼需要，便填寫。

options.en: The volunteer rejected the return record and refused any shared procedure.
options.zh: 義工拒絕歸還記錄，也拒絕任何共同程序。

scene.explanationZh: 他已問過並理解用途；有判斷後照做，不是自動盲從，也不是拒絕合作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能由反對 blind obedience 得出？

options.en: The person wants room to examine reasons and consequences.
options.zh: 那人想有空間檢視理由與後果。

options.en: The person must reject every instruction even after understanding a useful reason for it.
options.zh: 那人即使已理解有用理由，也必須拒絕每個指示。

options.en: The context can show how questions and cooperation coexist.
options.zh: 情境可以展示提問與合作怎樣並存。

contrast.explanationZh: 不盲從不等於一概拒絕；重點是理解與判斷，不是為反對而反對。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「團隊若可問圖說，就是不尊重編輯吧？」你想保留查證與合作。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Respect does not require blind obedience; we can explain a doubt about the evidence and still work towards the shared deadline.
options.zh: 尊重不要求盲從；我們可以解釋對證據的疑問，也仍朝共同期限合作。

options.en: I would avoid raising a doubtful date because agreeing with the editor matters more than checking this caption.
options.zh: 我會避免提出可疑日期，因為同意編輯比核對這段圖說更重要。

options.en: I would refuse the agreed deadline before discussing whether the caption itself can be checked.
options.zh: 我會先拒絕議定期限，不討論圖說本身能否核對。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以提出具體證據問題，也繼續協調；不必用沉默表示尊重，也不因有疑問就先取消共同安排。

speaking.en: I can cooperate without blind obedience by explaining the part I do not understand before agreeing to put my name to it.
speaking.zh: 我可以合作而不盲從，在同意署名前，先解釋自己不明白的部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把獨立判斷連到具體問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你負責檢討一項資料輸入流程。舊指引要求每欄填數字，但同事發現部分原始記錄根本沒有數值，仍照填零，令「未知」被誤當真實零值。用一至兩句英文實際提出修正：解釋問題，建議暫把缺漏標為未知並請負責人確認處理方式；不要指控同事故意造假，也不要取消全部核對程序。

examples.en: Blind obedience to the old form has turned missing values into zeros, so the report no longer shows which figures are unknown. I suggest marking those entries as unknown for now and asking the process owner to confirm how missing data should be handled.
examples.zh: 盲目遵從舊表格，令缺漏值變成了零，報告因而看不出哪些數字未知。我建議暫時把那些項目標為未知，並請流程負責人確認應怎樣處理缺漏資料。

examples.en: We should replace blind obedience to the numeric-only instruction with a documented way to record missing data. Could we flag the affected entries as unknown and ask for an approved procedure, while keeping the checks on the figures we actually have?
examples.zh: 我們應以有記錄可循的缺漏資料處理方法，取代對「只填數字」指引的盲從。我們可否把受影響項目標成未知，並請求確認程序，同時保留對實際已有數字的核對？

writing.selfCheckZh: 修正須連到零值與未知的實際差別，提出可查的暫記及確認方法；不把指引問題變成惡意指控，也不因反對盲從便取消有用核對。

takeaways.en: The class distinguished blind obedience from following a rule after understanding the shared problem it addressed.
takeaways.zh: 課堂把盲從，與理解規則處理的共同問題後才遵守，作出區分。

takeaways.en: She said that asking for the missing evidence was cooperation with judgement, not blind obedience or a refusal to help.
takeaways.zh: 她說，要求缺漏證據是有判斷的合作，不是盲從，也不是拒絕幫忙。

lessons.titleZh: 像持指南針的人一樣引導方向

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A good leader acts like holding a compass.

brief.meaningEn: In a leadership image, helping people orient towards a purpose as someone using a compass would, rather than forcing every choice.
brief.meaningZh: 在領導圖像中，像使用指南針的人一樣，幫大家朝目的辨認方向，而不強迫每個選擇。
brief.grammar: a leader is like someone holding a compass; picture the leader as a person holding a compass. Like compares a person with someone doing the action. Holding a compass can also be literal; the context must establish the guidance image.
brief.register: A productive navigation comparison, related to act like a compass but retaining the human holder who interprets direction. It is not a fixed whole idiom or a new dictionary sense for compass.
brief.boundaryZh: 有方向工具不等於已決定所有步驟，也不保證成功；普通照片中的指南針可以只是物件，不能自動當成領導能力證據。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把引導寫成替別人作每個決定，也不把任何出現指南針的情景都硬套成領導比喻。
brief.outcomeZh: 能交代圖像中的人物、工具及共同目的，並分清定向與控制。

listening.promptZh: 圖像中的領導者怎樣提供方向？

options.en: She helps the group compare possible routes against a shared purpose without making every step herself.
options.zh: 她幫小組按共同目的比較可能路線，不替他們決定每一步。

options.en: The essay describes her requiring the group to follow each of her choices without comparison.
options.zh: 文章描述她要求小組不作比較，跟從她每個選擇。

options.en: The image is used only to describe the physical object in a shop display, with no leadership meaning.
options.zh: 圖像只用來描述店舖展示中的實際物件，沒有領導意思。

options.en: The group has already completed the project, and the leader is only checking which route was fastest.
options.zh: 小組已完成項目，領導者只在核對哪條路最快。

listening.explanationZh: 保持共同目的並比較路線，是定向作用；不是逐步命令、純物件展示，也沒有交代項目已完成。
listening.en: The essay pictures the leader as someone holding a compass: she keeps the shared purpose in view and asks the group to compare routes, rather than deciding every step for them.
listening.zh: 文章把領導者描寫為持指南針的人：她讓大家記得共同目的，請小組比較路線，而不是替他們決定每一步。

reply.promptEn: How does the essay picture the leader’s contribution?
reply.promptZh: 文章怎樣描寫領導者的作用？

options.en: It pictures her as someone holding a compass, helping the group keep its purpose in view.
options.zh: 它把她描寫為持指南針的人，幫小組記得目的。

options.en: She gives orientation while leaving routes to be compared together.
options.zh: 她提供方向感，同時讓大家一起比較路線。

options.en: The group has guidance without having every practical choice made for it.
options.zh: 小組有引導，但不是每個實際選擇都由人代作。

options.en: Her questions connect possible actions with what the group is trying to achieve.
options.zh: 她的問題把可能行動，與小組想達到的目的連起來。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描寫定向與共同判斷，不把工具圖像說成已替人走完整段路。

scene.promptZh: 展板只有一張遊客手持指南針的照片，說明文字只記錄物件借用，沒有交代他怎樣帶領他人。有人只看照片便說已證明他擅長引導團隊。哪句謹慎？

options.en: A photograph of someone holding a compass can be literal; it does not by itself establish the guiding role imagined in the leadership comparison.
options.zh: 手持指南針的照片可以只是字面情景，本身不足以確立領導比喻中想像的引導角色。

options.en: The label already describes him helping a team compare actions against a shared aim.
options.zh: 說明文字已描述他幫團隊按共同目標比較行動。

options.en: Possession of the object is enough to establish how he listens to the people he leads.
options.zh: 持有物件，便足以確立他怎樣聆聽自己帶領的人。

scene.explanationZh: 物件照片與領導互動是不同證據；沒有具體引導資料，不能只按圖像補出能力。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能由領導者像 someone holding a compass 的比喻得出？

options.en: The image can suggest orientation towards a shared purpose.
options.zh: 圖像可表示朝共同目的定向。

options.en: The leader has already guaranteed the result and made every later choice unnecessary.
options.zh: 領導者已保證結果，讓後來所有選擇都不再需要。

options.en: The context should explain what purpose or questions provide direction.
options.zh: 情境應解釋甚麼目的或問題提供方向。

contrast.explanationZh: 提供方向不等於保證結果，也不取消大家仍需作的判斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然她帶方向，我們只抄她每個答案就好吧？」你想保留共同判斷。哪個回應最好？

options.en: The image of someone holding a compass is about orientation; we still need to compare what each option does for our shared aim.
options.zh: 持指南針者的圖像說的是定向；我們仍需要比較各選項怎樣服務共同目標。

options.en: I would use her preferred answer as the whole explanation, without discussing how it fits the aim.
options.zh: 我會把她偏好的答案當成全部解釋，不討論怎樣配合目標。

options.en: I would ignore her questions because making our own choice means accepting no guidance.
options.zh: 我會忽略她的問題，因為自行作選擇就表示不接受引導。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以借助問題和方向而保留選擇；不需照抄全部，也不因要自主便拒絕所有引導。

speaking.en: Our coordinator is like someone holding a compass, helping us ask which route serves the purpose before we choose the next step.
speaking.zh: 我們的協調員像持指南針的人，幫我們在選下一步前，先問哪條路服務目的。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把人與持工具的人作清楚比較。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們要為小組合作手冊設計一幅插圖，表現協調者提供方向而不操縱所有人。你想請畫師把協調者畫成持指南針的人，組員則各自拿着可比較的路線草圖；圖說要提共同目的，而不是唯一必勝路線。用一至兩句英文實際提出圖像與圖說建議。

examples.en: Could we picture the coordinator as someone holding a compass, with members comparing their own route sketches beside her? The caption could name the shared purpose without suggesting she has already chosen every step for them.
examples.zh: 我們可否把協調者畫成持指南針的人，組員在她旁邊比較各自的路線草圖？圖說可以指出共同目的，而不暗示她已替他們選好每一步。

examples.en: I suggest a figure holding a compass to represent orientation, alongside several members discussing possible routes. Let the caption connect their choices with the shared aim, rather than promise a single route that cannot fail.
examples.zh: 我建議用一個持指南針的人物表示定向，旁邊有幾位組員討論可能路線。讓圖說把選擇連到共同目標，而不是承諾一條不會失敗的唯一路線。

writing.selfCheckZh: 建議須有實際可畫的角色與比較活動，並用圖說交代共同目的；不把指南針當成控制所有人或保證結果的工具，也不只畫物件而沒有說明圖像作用。

takeaways.en: The story compares the mentor with someone holding a compass, asking what direction matters before the learner chooses how to proceed.
takeaways.zh: 故事把導師比作持指南針的人，先問甚麼方向重要，再由學員選擇怎樣繼續。

takeaways.en: In their poster, the person holding a compass represents shared orientation, while the different sketches leave room for discussion.
takeaways.zh: 在他們的海報裏，持指南針的人表示共同定向，不同草圖則保留討論空間。

lessons.titleZh: 粗聲厲氣地發號施令

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A good leader does not bark orders.

brief.meaningEn: Give commands in a loud, sharp or harsh manner.
brief.meaningZh: 用響亮、急厲或粗暴的語氣發出命令。
brief.grammar: bark orders at/to someone; barked, barking. The verb describes how speech is delivered, not whether its information is correct. Distinguish a firm, audible instruction from an aggressively snapped command.
brief.register: A conventional speech metaphor for forceful, harsh or aggressive commands. No literal animal action is needed.
brief.boundaryZh: 大聲可能為了讓人聽見，清楚堅定也不必粗暴；要有聲線、態度或互動線索，而不是只按音量、內容或職銜判斷。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把有用指示自動等同粗聲命令，也不因內容正確便否認語氣可能令人難以提問。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清語氣與指示內容，並在改寫或排演時用具體聲線及互動支持判斷。

listening.promptZh: 哪些線索說明了說話方式，而不是只指職責？

options.en: The supervisor used a sharp manner and shut down questions while the updated information was still missing.
options.zh: 主管用急厲語氣，並阻止提問，而更新資料仍未提供。

options.en: The supervisor calmly supplied the revised list and invited the crew to check it.
options.zh: 主管平靜地提供修訂清單，並請工作人員核對。

options.en: The crew had the revised list and were discussing it without interruption.
options.zh: 工作人員已有修訂清單，正不受打斷地討論。

options.en: The account concerns only the list’s contents, with no description of the supervisor’s tone.
options.zh: 敘述只談清單內容，沒有描述主管語氣。

listening.explanationZh: snapping 及打斷提問提供語氣與互動線索，不只是有指示；資料仍未送達，也不是平靜邀請核對。
listening.en: When the props were late, the supervisor began to bark orders, snapping at the crew and cutting off questions, even though nobody had been given the revised list.
listening.zh: 道具遲到時，主管開始粗聲發號施令，厲聲對待工作人員並打斷問題，雖然根本沒有人收到修訂清單。

reply.promptEn: How did the supervisor respond to the delay?
reply.promptZh: 主管怎樣回應延誤？

options.en: The supervisor began to bark orders and cut off the crew’s questions.
options.zh: 主管開始粗聲發號施令，打斷工作人員的提問。

options.en: The response was sharp and left little space to clarify the missing list.
options.zh: 回應急厲，幾乎沒有空間釐清缺漏清單。

options.en: The supervisor snapped at people rather than first supplying the updated information.
options.zh: 主管厲聲對待大家，而不是先提供更新資料。

options.en: The account describes a harsh delivery, not just a clear instruction.
options.zh: 敘述描述粗暴的說話方式，不只是清楚指示。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體語氣及互動回答，不把職責本身當成粗暴的證據。

scene.promptZh: 場地很嘈，協調員提高聲量讓遠處聽見，仍用尊重語氣解釋集合點，並停下回答問題。評論只按聲量便說她粗聲發令。哪句最好？

options.en: Raising her voice to be heard does not by itself show that she barked orders; the account also describes respectful explanation and questions.
options.zh: 為了讓人聽見而提高聲量，本身不足以顯示她粗聲發令；敘述也交代尊重的解釋及提問。

options.en: The account says she snapped at people and refused to hear any question.
options.zh: 敘述說，她厲聲對待大家，拒絕聽任何問題。

options.en: The instruction is described as inaudible to distant participants rather than deliberately made clearer.
options.zh: 指示被描述為遠處參加者聽不見，而不是刻意說得更清楚。

scene.explanationZh: 音量與粗暴態度不同；要看整體語氣及是否容許釐清，不能只按嘈雜環境下說得較響來判斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「He barked orders」得出？

options.en: He gave commands in a harsh or sharply forceful manner.
options.zh: 他用粗暴或急厲有力的方式發命令。

options.en: Every factual detail in the commands was therefore false.
options.zh: 命令中的每項事實資料，因此都是錯的。

options.en: More context can explain what he said and how others responded.
options.zh: 更多情境可以交代他說甚麼及別人怎樣回應。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語描述說話方式，不能單憑語氣判斷全部內容真假；正確資訊也可以被粗暴地說出。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只要指示內容正確，就不用再管他怎樣說吧？」工作人員還需要問修訂清單。哪個回應最好？

options.en: Even correct information can be delivered by someone who barks orders; we still need a way to hear and clarify the revised list without being cut off.
options.zh: 即使資訊正確，說話者也可能粗聲發令；我們仍需要能聽清並釐清修訂清單，而不被打斷的方法。

options.en: I would use the accuracy of the list as the only measure and leave the tone out of the discussion.
options.zh: 我會只用清單準確性作指標，不討論語氣。

options.en: I would reject the revised details because the harsh delivery alone shows they cannot be useful.
options.zh: 我會拒絕修訂資料，因為單是粗暴說法就顯示它們不可能有用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應分清資訊內容與互動方式；不因一方面便抹去另一面，也不只用語氣否定全部有用資訊。

speaking.en: We can give a clear instruction without having to bark orders, and leave enough space for someone to ask about an unclear detail.
speaking.zh: 我們可以清楚交代指示，不必粗聲發號施令，也留下足夠空間讓人詢問不清楚的細節。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清堅定、清楚與粗暴。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替短劇排演提供筆記。這場戲的角色是請老朋友幫忙找一封信，想表現信任而非支配；演員卻把台詞讀成怒斥命令。用一至兩句英文實際給演員建議，說明這個說法會怎樣改變關係，並請試用邀請而非厲聲命令的語氣，不要求整場只能小聲。

examples.en: If you bark orders here, the request will sound like control rather than trust between old friends. Could we try the line as an invitation to help find the letter, with a clear voice and room for the other character to answer?
examples.zh: 若你在這裏粗聲發號施令，請求就會像控制，不是老朋友之間的信任。我們可否把這句試成邀請對方幫忙找信，聲音清楚，也讓另一角色有空間回答？

examples.en: The character is asking an old friend for help, so please do not bark orders in this exchange. I suggest keeping the words audible but softening the attack in the delivery, so the reply can feel like a choice rather than submission.
examples.zh: 角色在向老朋友求助，所以這段交流請不要粗聲發號施令。我建議把字句說得聽得見，但減去說法中的攻擊感，讓回覆感覺像一個選擇，而不是屈服。

writing.selfCheckZh: 筆記要連到這場戲的關係與台詞意圖，提出可試的具體說法；不只叫人小聲，也不因反對粗暴就讓台詞聽不清楚。

takeaways.en: The organiser did not need to bark orders to explain the change; a clear pause and a chance for questions made the new arrangement understandable.
takeaways.zh: 主辦者不用粗聲發令也能解釋改動；清楚停頓及提問機會，讓新安排容易理解。

takeaways.en: The narrator notices when the captain starts barking orders, contrasting the sharp delivery with the careful explanation offered earlier.
takeaways.zh: 敘述者留意隊長開始粗聲發令，把急厲說法與較早的仔細解釋對比。

lessons.titleZh: 以行為贏得別人的信任

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Leaders must earn people's trust.

brief.meaningEn: Gain other people’s confidence through conduct they find reliable or worthy of belief.
brief.meaningZh: 透過別人認為可靠或值得相信的行為，逐漸取得他們的信任。
brief.grammar: earn people’s trust; earned, earning. Earn here concerns gaining confidence through behaviour, not purchasing a guaranteed response. People’s is possessive; those people still decide whom to trust.
brief.register: A natural verb-object collocation. Explain the behaviour and the people concerned rather than infer trust from a title, an appeal or the mere promise to be trustworthy.
brief.boundaryZh: 嘗試贏得不等於已取得所有人的信任，也不表示從此不能被質疑；需要可檢視的行為及持續跟進。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把要求別人相信當成已贏得，也不把信任當成可以略過核對或自願同意的理由。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出具體、可查的可靠行動，同時保留別人提問及自行判斷的權利。

listening.promptZh: 她怎樣嘗試建立信任？

options.en: She made the correction available for checking and explained what had gone wrong.
options.zh: 她公開更正供人核對，並解釋出了甚麼錯。

options.en: She asked people to trust her title without seeing the corrected record.
options.zh: 她請大家只相信職銜，不看更正記錄。

options.en: She withheld the changed list until everyone had promised to accept her account.
options.zh: 她把更正清單留着，直到每個人都答應接受她的說法。

options.en: The account confirms that every person now trusts her and will not question another decision.
options.zh: 敘述確認每個人現在都信任她，以後不再質疑其他決定。

listening.explanationZh: 公布可查資料及解釋錯誤，是具體行動；tried 不保證所有人已信任，也沒有取消後續提問。
listening.en: The organiser tried to earn people’s trust by publishing the corrected list and explaining the error; she did not ask them to accept her assurances before they could check the change.
listening.zh: 主辦者嘗試透過公布更正清單及解釋錯誤，贏得別人的信任；她沒有要求大家在核對改動前，先接受她的保證。

reply.promptEn: What did the organiser do to build confidence after the error?
reply.promptZh: 出錯後，主辦者做了甚麼來建立信心？

options.en: She tried to earn people’s trust through an explanation and a corrected list they could check.
options.zh: 她嘗試以解釋及可核對的更正清單，贏得別人的信任。

options.en: She let people inspect the change instead of relying only on her assurance.
options.zh: 她讓大家查看改動，不只依賴她的保證。

options.en: The error was acknowledged in a way others could examine for themselves.
options.zh: 錯誤以別人可自行檢視的方式得到承認。

options.en: She gave the correction and its reason, while leaving people able to check them.
options.zh: 她提供更正及理由，也讓大家能核對。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出可檢視的行動，不只自稱可靠或要求別人停止提問。

scene.promptZh: 一位新負責人只在介紹中說「你們應該信我，因為我有這個職銜」，尚未提供行動、說明或工作記錄。宣傳卻說他已贏得大家信任。哪句謹慎？

options.en: The title and request alone do not show that he has earned people’s trust through reliable conduct.
options.zh: 單是職銜及信任要求，不足以顯示他已透過可靠行為贏得大家信任。

options.en: The introduction describes a completed correction that members could inspect.
options.zh: 介紹描述了一項已完成、會員可查看的更正。

options.en: The account reports members’ confidence based on a sustained record of keeping commitments.
options.zh: 敘述報告會員基於持續履行承諾的記錄而產生信心。

scene.explanationZh: 有職銜或提出要求，不是已表現可靠行為及得到信任的證據；不能自行補出更正或長期記錄。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「She hopes to earn people’s trust」得出？

options.en: She wants to gain others’ confidence through how she acts.
options.zh: 她希望透過自己的行為，得到別人的信心。

options.en: Everyone has already agreed to trust her without further questions.
options.zh: 每個人已同意不再提問便相信她。

options.en: More context could describe the commitments and actions involved.
options.zh: 更多情境可以交代涉及的承諾及行動。

contrast.explanationZh: 希望與已達成不同；信任也不需要別人放棄查看或提問。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「她已解釋過，就要求大家別再查清單，才算信任吧？」你想保留信任與核對。哪個回應最好？

options.en: She can earn people’s trust by making the correction checkable; allowing questions supports that process rather than cancelling it.
options.zh: 她可以透過讓更正可核對，贏得別人的信任；容許問題支持這個過程，而不是取消它。

options.en: I would remove access to the list after the explanation, so people could show confidence by not checking.
options.zh: 我會在解釋後取消查看清單的方法，讓大家以不核對來表示信心。

options.en: I would count the explanation itself as confirmation that every person now agrees with her next decision.
options.zh: 我會把這次解釋本身，當成每個人都已同意她下一個決定的確認。

dialogue.explanationZh: 讓人可查及提問，是建立可靠性的具體方式；不是限制資料，也不能把一次解釋擴成未來決定全獲同意。

speaking.en: I hope to earn people’s trust by keeping the commitments I make and explaining clearly when something has to change.
speaking.zh: 我希望透過履行承諾，以及在需要改變時清楚解釋，贏得別人的信任。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把信任連到可持續檢視的行為。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你剛獲選為小組協調員，要向會員發第一則介紹訊息。你不能要求因職銜便信任，想說明會把決定及理由記下供人查看，引用會員故事前先問本人，並提供提問方法。用一至兩句英文實際寫介紹，不保證每人都立即相信你。

examples.en: I hope to earn people’s trust by keeping a record of decisions and reasons that members can read, and by asking before using anyone’s story. Please send me questions through this group or speak with me after the meeting; the title alone is not a reason to stop asking.
examples.zh: 我希望透過保留會員可查看的決定及理由記錄，以及使用任何人的故事前先詢問，贏得大家信任。請在這個群組發問題，或在聚會後找我談；職銜本身不是停止提問的理由。

examples.en: Being chosen does not automatically earn people’s trust, so I want to make my commitments clear: readable decision notes and permission before sharing personal accounts. You can ask me here or after a meeting, and I will explain what I can and what still needs checking.
examples.zh: 獲選不會自動贏得大家信任，所以我想說清承諾：可供閱讀的決定筆記，以及分享個人敘述前先取得許可。你可以在這裏或聚會後提問，我會說明已知的內容及仍需核對的地方。

glossary.en: a record of decisions and reasons

glossary.zh: 使用任何人的故事之前

writing.selfCheckZh: 介紹要給具體可查的承諾、故事使用界線及提問方法；以後仍要實際履行，不把當選當成信任已完成，也不替會員預定感受。

takeaways.en: The repair team earned people’s trust by returning with the promised update, including the part they had not yet resolved.
takeaways.zh: 維修團隊按承諾帶回更新，包括仍未解決的部分，因而贏得別人的信任。

takeaways.en: She wanted to earn people’s trust through a consistent record, not by treating a difficult question as disloyalty.
takeaways.zh: 她想透過一致的記錄贏得大家信任，不把困難問題當成不忠。

Main checkable correction after error, inverse title/request with no conduct is not earned confidence, final actual new-coordinator introduction offers prospective decision-note access, permission and question channels rather than retelling an existing correction.

lessons.titleZh: 按目前情況而言

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: As things stand now, the project will begin in June.

brief.meaningEn: Given the situation at the present time, leaving room for later changes.
brief.meaningZh: 按目前的情況來說，同時保留之後可能改變。
brief.grammar: as things stand now, + statement; often an opening qualifier, also possible after a clause. Things stand refers to the current state, not objects physically standing. Now does not make the statement a permanent guarantee.
brief.register: A natural present-situation qualification. State what is known or expected at this point, and distinguish a later update from claiming the earlier statement was timeless.
brief.boundaryZh: 目前預計不等於不可改，也不表示已發生；需要交代適用時間及仍有的條件，收到更新時重新評估。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把舊時點的計劃當成最新資料，也不因仍可改變就說目前甚麼都不能交代。
brief.outcomeZh: 能清楚報告目前範圍，保留未定部分，並說明甚麼資料會更新判斷。

listening.promptZh: 目前可交代甚麼？哪項仍未確定？

options.en: Friday is the current return plan, while the person collecting the screens is still being checked.
options.zh: 星期五是目前歸還計劃，領取屏風的人則仍在確認。

options.en: The screens have already been returned and the message only records the completed handover.
options.zh: 屏風已歸還，訊息只記錄完成的交接。

options.en: The collecting person has been confirmed, while there is no proposed return day.
options.zh: 領取者已確認，卻沒有擬定歸還日。

options.en: The organiser has promised the plan cannot change if new information arrives.
options.zh: 主辦者已承諾，即使收到新資料，計劃也不會改變。

listening.explanationZh: 目前計劃與已完成不同；待核領取者仍是條件，開頭也沒有把計劃變成不可更新的承諾。
listening.en: As things stand now, the borrowed screens can return on Friday, but the organiser is still checking who can collect them; the message gives the current plan rather than a completed return.
listening.zh: 按目前情況，借來的屏風可在星期五歸還，但主辦者仍在確認誰能領取；訊息交代的是目前計劃，不是已完成歸還。

reply.promptEn: What can you say about the return arrangement at this point?
reply.promptZh: 在這個時點，你可以怎樣交代歸還安排？

options.en: As things stand now, Friday is possible, but the collecting person still needs confirmation.
options.zh: 按目前情況，星期五可以，但領取者仍需確認。

options.en: The current plan is Friday, with one practical detail still being checked.
options.zh: 目前計劃是星期五，還有一項實際詳情在核對。

options.en: We have a proposed day, not a record that the screens are already back.
options.zh: 我們有擬定日期，不是屏風已送回的記錄。

options.en: The organiser can report the present plan while making clear that collection has not been fully arranged.
options.zh: 主辦者可以交代目前計劃，同時說清領取仍未完全安排好。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說清目前已知及未定部分，不把它說成已完成或永久保證。

scene.promptZh: 周一通知說當時房間仍在維修，周三新通知已確認重開。有人只引用周一的「按目前情況」就說周三也不能使用。哪句最好？

options.en: A statement about how things stood on Monday does not replace the confirmed Wednesday update; we should report the current position.
options.zh: 周一情況的說明，不能取代周三已確認的更新；應報告目前狀況。

options.en: The Monday qualifier makes the earlier repair status permanent despite the later confirmed reopening.
options.zh: 周一的限定語讓當時維修狀態永久不變，即使後來已確認重開。

options.en: The Wednesday notice is described as an unconfirmed hope, rather than a confirmed reopening.
options.zh: 敘述把周三通知說成未確認的希望，而不是已確認重開。

scene.explanationZh: 時點限定容許更新，不能讓舊狀態壓過後來確定資料；也不能把已確認改寫成只是希望。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能只從「As things stand now, we plan to start next week」得出？

options.en: Next week is the plan given the present situation.
options.zh: 按目前情況，下周是計劃開始時間。

options.en: The start has already happened and no later information can affect it.
options.zh: 開始已發生，而且任何後來資料都不能影響。

options.en: A later update may revise the plan if the situation changes.
options.zh: 若情況改變，後來更新可能修訂計劃。

contrast.explanationZh: plan 不是已發生，now 是目前範圍，不是排除以後更新。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「仍在核對，就乾脆別說星期五，讓大家猜吧？」你想有界限地報告已知進度。哪個回應最好？

options.en: As things stand now, Friday is the plan; we can say that and clearly identify the collection detail still being checked.
options.zh: 按目前情況，星期五是計劃；我們可以這樣交代，並清楚指出領取詳情仍在核對。

options.en: I would withhold the proposed day until every detail is fixed, even though people need the current plan to arrange their time.
options.zh: 即使大家需要目前計劃來安排時間，我也會等所有詳情定好才透露擬定日期。

options.en: I would announce Friday as a completed handover so nobody needs to ask about collection.
options.zh: 我會把星期五公布成已完成交接，讓大家不用再問領取。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可清楚分開已知計劃及未定詳情，不用隱去全部資訊，也不能為避免問題便把計劃說成已完成。

speaking.en: As things stand now, I can describe the agreed part of the plan and tell you which details still need confirmation.
speaking.zh: 按目前情況，我可以交代計劃中已議定的部分，也說明哪些詳情仍需確認。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把目前資料與待核部分分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你跟伙伴在寫懸疑故事閱讀札記。到目前一章，只知道一張紙條出現在空房，尚未知道誰放的，也沒有看過下一章。伙伴想直接指認一位角色。用一至兩句英文實際記下目前可支持的判斷，提議繼續查讀敘述時間及角色行動，而不是先下定論。

examples.en: As things stand now, we know where the note was found, not who put it there. I would compare the sequence and the characters’ movements in the next chapter before our notes identify a character as the person who left it.
examples.zh: 按目前情況，我們知道紙條在哪裏被發現，不知道是誰放的。我會先比較下一章的先後次序及角色行動，再在札記中指認留下紙條的人。

examples.en: As things stand now, the empty room is part of the evidence, but it does not identify who left the note there. Let us keep the conclusion open while we check the timing and what each character could actually have done.
examples.zh: 按目前情況，空房是證據的一部分，卻未能指出是誰把紙條留下。我們查讀時間及各角色實際可能做過甚麼時，先讓結論保持未定吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 札記要以目前章節的已知證據限制結論，給出接下來查讀的具體方向；不知道是誰留下，不等於沒有任何線索，也不能以伙伴直覺當已指認的證據。

takeaways.en: As things stand now, the two accounts agree on the date but not the order of the visits, so the editor keeps that point open.
takeaways.zh: 按目前情況，兩份敘述的日期相同，但探訪次序不同，所以編輯把那點保留未定。

takeaways.en: As things stand now, the group can offer one session, and it will review a second only after asking who is available.
takeaways.zh: 按目前情況，小組可以提供一場活動，詢問誰有空後才再考慮第二場。

lessons.titleZh: 學習、放下舊觀念，再重新學習

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Good leaders must learn, unlearn, and relearn.

brief.meaningEn: Gain knowledge or skills, let go of an outdated assumption or habit, and learn again in a changed way.
brief.meaningZh: 取得知識或技能、放下不再適合的假設或習慣，再以改變了的方式重新學習。
brief.grammar: learn, unlearn, and relearn is a parallel three-verb sequence; use with have to/need to/can. Unlearn concerns revising a learned assumption or habit, not literally erasing all memory or denying every earlier skill.
brief.register: A memorable natural parallel sequence, not an opaque idiom or an attributed quotation in this lesson. State what is being learned, questioned and practised differently.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是所有舊知識都要丟掉，也不只把相同步驟做得更快；需要具體新資料、被修正的假設及新的練習方式。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把承認需要重學當成以前全無能力，也不把三個動詞當沒有內容的口號。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體經驗說明觀念與做法怎樣修訂，並保留仍有用的基礎。

listening.promptZh: 這三個動詞在敘述中各有甚麼具體內容？

options.en: She gained new knowledge, questioned an earlier interpretation of quietness and practised different ways to check understanding.
options.zh: 她取得新知識，質疑以前對安靜的解讀，再練習不同的理解確認方法。

options.en: She repeated the old assumption more quickly without examining how the new pupils communicated.
options.zh: 她更快地重複舊假設，沒有檢視新學生怎樣溝通。

options.en: She discarded every teaching skill she had and stopped checking pupils’ understanding.
options.zh: 她丟掉所有已有教學技能，停止確認學生是否理解。

options.en: The new class had already been assessed using one unchanged method, and no further learning was described.
options.zh: 新班已用一個不變方法完成評核，敘述沒有交代進一步學習。

listening.explanationZh: 三個部分都有內容：了解語言、修正安靜的假設、重練確認方法；不是全部丟掉，也不是原樣重複。
listening.en: In the new class, she had to learn, unlearn, and relearn: find out how pupils used several languages, question her assumption that quiet meant confusion, and practise checking understanding in different ways.
listening.zh: 在新班裏，她需要學習、放下舊觀念，再重新學習：了解學生怎樣使用幾種語言，質疑自己把安靜當成困惑的假設，並練習用不同方法確認理解。

reply.promptEn: What did adapting to the new class involve?
reply.promptZh: 適應新班涉及甚麼？

options.en: She had to learn, unlearn, and relearn, including revising what she thought a quiet response meant.
options.zh: 她需要學習、放下舊觀念，再重新學習，包括修訂自己對安靜回應的理解。

options.en: She learned about the pupils’ languages and stopped assuming that quietness always signalled confusion.
options.zh: 她了解學生的語言，也不再假定安靜總表示困惑。

options.en: New information changed an earlier interpretation and led to different checking practices.
options.zh: 新資料改變了以前的解讀，並帶來不同的確認做法。

options.en: She kept developing her teaching by asking different questions rather than simply repeating the same assumption.
options.zh: 她透過不同提問繼續發展教學，而不只重複相同假設。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述有內容的調整，不把重學當失去所有基礎，也不只說多做幾次。

scene.promptZh: 義工一直按同一份已確認清單摺傳單，現在做得更快；敘述沒有新資料、假設修正或方法改動。簡介卻稱這已完整展示三段學習循環。哪句謹慎？

options.en: Faster repetition alone does not show someone working through a cycle of “learn, unlearn, and relearn”; the account gives no revised assumption or approach.
options.zh: 單是更快重複，沒有展示學習、放下舊觀念、再重新學習的完整過程；敘述沒有指出被修訂的假設或方法。

options.en: The account identifies a new rule that replaced the earlier folding method.
options.zh: 敘述指出一條取代原摺法的新規則。

options.en: The volunteer has stopped using the confirmed list because new evidence showed it was outdated.
options.zh: 義工因新證據顯示清單過時，已停止使用它。

scene.explanationZh: 熟練重複可以有價值，但不自動包括放下舊觀念及改變方法；不能補出新規則或清單過時。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不能由 learn, unlearn, and relearn 得出？

options.en: New learning can include revising an earlier assumption or habit.
options.zh: 新的學習可以包括修訂以前的假設或習慣。

options.en: Every earlier skill must be erased before anything new can be learned.
options.zh: 必須先抹掉所有舊技能，才能學任何新事物。

options.en: The context should show what is being questioned and practised differently.
options.zh: 情境應展示甚麼受到質疑，以及練習怎樣不同。

contrast.explanationZh: 放下不合用假設，不等於刪去全部技能；新舊基礎可以經檢視後重新結合。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「她以前不是教過書嗎？還要重學就證明以前甚麼都不懂吧？」你想說明具體調整。哪個回應最好？

options.en: She can learn, unlearn, and relearn while keeping useful experience; the change concerns an assumption about quiet pupils, not the loss of all teaching knowledge.
options.zh: 她可以學習、放下舊觀念、再重學，同時保留有用經驗；這次改變關乎對安靜學生的假設，不是失去全部教學知識。

options.en: I would describe the new class as proof that none of her earlier experience can be useful.
options.zh: 我會把新班當成她以前沒有任何經驗可用的證據。

options.en: I would keep the earlier interpretation of quietness unchanged and focus only on making the same explanation louder.
options.zh: 我會原樣保留以前對安靜的解讀，只把相同解釋說得更響。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可保留基礎，也針對新資料修正假設；不是全部否定，也不是只改音量而不改理解。

speaking.en: I need to learn, unlearn, and relearn when new evidence changes an assumption, while keeping the skills that still help me ask careful questions.
speaking.zh: 新證據改變假設時，我需要學習、放下舊觀念，再重學，同時保留仍能幫我仔細提問的技能。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明修訂哪項假設及仍保留甚麼。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你整理家族物件時，曾以為「以前由誰擁有」就等於「由誰製作」。新信件卻顯示那是一份禮物。你要寫一至兩句實際工作日記，記下新學到的來源、放下的假設，以及之後寫標籤前會怎樣核對；不把這次修正說成所有舊記錄都沒用。

examples.en: I have had to learn, unlearn, and relearn while tracing this object: the letter shows it was a gift, not something its owner necessarily made. I will separate ownership from authorship in the label and check the evidence for each, rather than discard every earlier record.
examples.zh: 追查這件物件時，我需要學習、放下舊觀念，再重新學習：信件顯示它是禮物，不一定由擁有者製作。我會在標籤分清擁有與製作，分別核對證據，而不丟掉每份舊記錄。

examples.en: Today I saw why I need to learn, unlearn, and relearn: I had treated an owner’s name as the maker’s, until the gift letter challenged that assumption. My next label will distinguish the two roles and state what is still unknown.
examples.zh: 今天我明白為甚麼自己需要學習、放下舊觀念，再重新學習：我曾把擁有者名字當成製作者，直到贈禮信件質疑了那個假設。下一張標籤會分清兩種角色，並交代仍未知甚麼。

writing.selfCheckZh: 日記要有新資料、被修正的假設及下一次標籤的具體查證方式；不把擁有者改成另一個未證實的製作者，也不因一點修正便否定全部記錄。

takeaways.en: The new evidence made the curator learn, unlearn, and relearn, changing one attribution without pretending the collection had no reliable history.
takeaways.zh: 新證據讓策展人學習、放下舊觀念、再重學，改變一項歸屬判斷，而不假裝整個收藏都沒有可靠歷史。

takeaways.en: To learn, unlearn, and relearn, the group compared its old assumption with the new accounts before deciding what to practise differently.
takeaways.zh: 為了學習、放下舊觀念、再重學，小組先把舊假設與新敘述比較，再決定怎樣改變練習。
